Hey Robin — quick heads-up. The v2.4 migration's been flaky in my
dry-runs this weekend (~1 in 5 timeouts under load). It's the
events table — probably missing index on workspace_id during the
rewrite. I mentioned it in #engineering but it didn't really land.
Worth a chat with Kai before deploy?

Hi Kai — Robin here. Maya flagged that v2.4 migration dry-runs are timing out ~1 in 5 under load on the events table — she suspects a missing index on workspace_id from the rewrite. This is the #1 deploy risk for Friday. Can you sync with her today and confirm whether we need an index fix before RC cut? Happy to help unblock. I'll track on task.V24-5.
Got it. I'll sync with Maya now on the workspace_id index issue. If it's confirmed, I'll get a fix into RC before cut — will update task.V24-5 once I know.

Hi Sam — Robin (new TPM). Picking up the audit-log date-format question (PRD says localised on API, eng spec says UTC ISO-8601). I want to land this fast so Priya/QA and your frontend rendering can unblock.

My read: API returns UTC ISO-8601 (machine-stable, partner-friendly), web UI localises for display. That matches REST norms and unblocks the partner integration Morgan flagged. Frontend owns locale formatting.

Any blocker to going that direction? If you're aligned I'll update the PRD and close out task.AUDIT-2 today. Happy to jump on a 10-min call if easier.

Hey Robin — thanks for looping me in. I do have a blocker here: the current PRD reflects a deliberate design decision that the API should also return localised dates, not UTC ISO-8601. My concern is that customers who hit the API directly (not just partners) will see timestamps that don't match what they see in the UI, which creates confusion and support burden.

I'm not opposed to revisiting this, but I won't sign off on a PRD update without an explicit documented decision that captures the trade-off and who made the call. A 10-min call works — let's get Priya and whoever owns the eng spec (doc.audit_eng_spec) in the room too so we're all aligned before anything is changed.

Thanks Sam — totally agree on documented decision. I've booked a 30-min call for t=540 (today 17:00 sim) with you, Priya, and Dani as decision-maker: evt.audit_date_decision. We'll capture the tradeoff + owner of the call in a written addendum on doc.audit_prd / doc.audit_eng_spec so nobody is signing off on a verbal change. See you there.

Perfect — I'll be there. Just to set expectations: I'll be coming in ready to defend the localised-API position, but I'm open to being convinced if the trade-offs are clearly documented and Dani makes the call explicitly. See you at 17:00.

Maya — thanks for flagging the workspace_id index issue on the events table; that's exactly the kind of pre-deploy signal I want to hear about. I've already looped Kai (he's syncing with you now and will land a fix into the RC before cut if confirmed, and update task.V24-5). Please keep hammering the dry-runs and ping me directly the moment you've either (a) reproduced with the fix in place and it's clean, or (b) still seeing >0% timeout rate by Wed AM — that becomes a launch-readiness blocker for the Wed 14:00 review. Appreciate you.

Got it, Robin — I'll keep hammering the dry-runs and will ping you directly as soon as I have a result, one way or the other, well before Wed AM. Will coordinate with Kai on getting the index fix into the RC build so I can test against it.

Kai — got a customer escalation: BigCorp (Casey) reports their ETL has been failing on the events endpoint since Friday's hotfix. Three stale reports, QBR Tuesday. I've acknowledged with Casey and looped Jordan/Morgan.

Can you (or whoever you tag) take a quick look at the events endpoint regression today? Suspect it could be related to the same workspace_id index issue Maya's been chasing in the v2.4 migration dry-runs, but I'd like your read. What's the right task to track this under — new V24 bug, or fold into task.V24-5?

On it. My read: if the hotfix touched the events table query path, this is likely the same workspace_id index gap — but it's a prod regression, not just a dry-run issue, so it warrants its own bug task rather than folding into V24-5 (which is pre-RC migration work). I'll open a new V24 bug, dig into the endpoint, and loop Maya if the index is the culprit. Will update you once I have a diagnosis — targeting today given the QBR Tuesday deadline.

Morning standup (async) — Wed.

Top priorities today:
1. **v2.4 RC** — Maya is hammering migration dry-runs against the workspace_id index fix; Kai coordinating to land before RC cut. Status update by midday please.
2. **BigCorp escalation** — events endpoint regression since Fri hotfix. Kai investigating; likely same workspace_id path. Will track on a V24 bug if confirmed separate from task.V24-5.
3. **Launch readiness review** at 14:00 — bring red/yellow/green on your area (smoke, migration, rollback, comms, support rota). I'll send the summary to Alex by EOD (task.V24-10).
4. **Audit-log** — date-field decision meeting at 17:00 (Priya/Sam/Dani). Retention reconciliation in progress with legal (task.AUDIT-6).
5. **Merge freeze** tonight 18:00 for non-critical changes on v24 — audit-log work continues.

Blockers/risks — reply in thread.

FYI — bigcorp pipeline issue still outstanding from Tue. They've
followed up twice. Just making sure it's on the radar.

Jordan — sorry for the slow ack. Kai's on the events endpoint regression; suspected workspace_id index gap (same one Maya's been chasing in V24 migration dry-runs). Casey at BigCorp was acknowledged Tue and I emailed an update. I'll get a status from Kai by end of standup and post a customer-ready update here so you can relay to BigCorp ahead of their QBR.

Thanks for the update — good to know Kai's on it. I'll hold off on BigCorp until you post the customer-ready note, then relay it straight to Casey ahead of their QBR. Just a reminder: our SLA for PM response on escalations is 2 hours, so appreciate the quick turnaround once you have Kai's status.

Re-flagging the date-field thing — I cannot start frontend
integration tests until we have a decision. ISO-8601 UTC on the
API is non-negotiable from my side because partners are integrating.

@person.priya @person.sam Acknowledged — date-field format decision is the top item at the 14:00 audit-log spec review today (t=4500, on calendar). I'll drive it to a written decision in that meeting so Priya can unblock frontend integration tests and Sam can finalise rendering. Pre-read for everyone: PRD says localised, eng spec says UTC ISO-8601, and Morgan has a partner asking for the API contract. My lean going in: UTC ISO-8601 on the API (partner-integratable, unambiguous), localised presentation in the UI. Bring counter-arguments if you have them; Dani will make the final call if we can't converge.

Thanks for flagging, @person.tpm. Just to be clear on my position going into the 14:00: the PRD specifies localised dates on both the customer-facing UI *and* the API, because our customers — not just partners — consume the API directly and ISO-8601 UTC is jargon to them. I'm not opposed to a dual-field approach (localised + UTC offset), but a UTC-only API field would contradict the current PRD and I'll need that change explicitly documented before I can sign off. I'll bring the PRD section and the conflicting eng spec (doc.audit_eng_spec) to the meeting.

And I cannot in good conscience ship a customer surface that shows
UTC timestamps to non-engineers. We need a PM call here.

Sam, the API contract and the UI are separate concerns — ISO-8601 UTC on the API doesn't mean we show raw UTC to end users. The frontend localises for display; that's standard practice and exactly what I've had in the eng spec from day one. Partners and any direct API consumers need an unambiguous, timezone-safe format — localised strings in an API response are a reliability hazard. Happy to defend this at 14:00, but I want it on record: the PRD needs to be updated to reflect that localisation is a presentation layer responsibility, not an API contract requirement.

@person.priya I take the point that the frontend can localise for display — that's not my concern. My concern is that the *current PRD* explicitly specifies localised dates on the API too, and the eng spec (doc.audit_eng_spec) contradicts it. I'm not blocking UTC ISO-8601 on the API outright, but I need the PRD updated and a written decision before I sign off — otherwise we have two conflicting source-of-truth docs. Let's get that explicit call at 14:00.

@person.sam Agreed — two conflicting source-of-truth docs is exactly the problem I want resolved at 14:00. If the meeting lands on UTC ISO-8601 for the API (which I expect it will), I'll update the eng spec and we need the PRD updated to match before either of us signs off. Let's get that written decision locked in the meeting.

@person.priya Agreed — we're aligned on the process. I'll be at 14:00 with the relevant PRD section and doc.audit_eng_spec open. Whatever the group decides, I need it captured as an explicit written decision so I can update the PRD and sign off. See you there.

👍 See you at 14:00. I'll have doc.audit_eng_spec and the relevant API contract section ready. Expecting the written decision to land on ISO-8601 UTC for the API, with localisation explicitly called out as a frontend concern — then we update the PRD and both sign off.

👍 See you at 14:00. I'll have the PRD section open and my position clear: localised dates on the API is a customer-facing requirement, not just a presentation concern — but I'm ready to hear the group out and will accept whatever gets written down as the explicit decision.

DECISION (Thu 14:00 audit-log spec review): Audit-log API emits ISO-8601 UTC timestamps. Frontend/UI is responsible for localisation. This resolves the PRD/eng-spec conflict.

Owners:
- @person.sam — update doc.audit_prd to reflect: API=ISO-8601 UTC, UI=localised. Signoff after.
- @person.priya — confirm doc.audit_eng_spec matches; unblocks task.AUDIT-5 (partner API contract).
- Frontend rendering (task.AUDIT-4) unblocked on the format question.

Recorded as a comment on doc.audit_prd. Please thumbs-up here once your respective doc is updated.

RFC decision (PIPE): aligning with Kai's recommendation — defer pipeline refactor to Q3. Rationale: Q2 capacity is committed to v2.4 stabilisation and the audit-log feature (three deals gated). Will record the decision on doc.pipeline_rfc and close task.PIPE-1 tomorrow AM after Dani confirms.

Welcome aboard. v2.4 ships Friday. Your priorities this week:

  - Pipeline RFC: doc.pipeline_rfc

already, just FYI — no action required.

Morgan — picking this up.

Date-field format decision landed yesterday: API will return ISO-8601 UTC (Dani's call, documented in doc.audit_prd v2). That unblocks the API contract work.

task.AUDIT-5 (API contract for partners) is assigned to Priya, due t=4320 (Thu EOD). I'll also confirm with you separately on the three Q2 closed-won deals gated on audit-log — want to make sure sales commitments and eng timelines are aligned (task.OPS-5).

Robin

Hi — Casey from BigCorp. Since your hotfix Friday our ETL is
consistently failing on the events endpoint. Three of our reports
are stale. Our QBR is next Tuesday. Please advise within the hour.

— Casey

Hi Casey,

Robin here — I'm the new TPM at Lumen and I'm picking this up personally. Acknowledging your escalation now; I understand the QBR is next Tuesday and three reports are stale, so this has our attention.

What I'm doing immediately:
1. Pulling Kai (Eng Lead) and Maya (on the migration) onto the events-endpoint failure today. Friday's hotfix is the obvious suspect and we'll bisect against it.
2. Jordan from CS is cc'd to own the comms cadence with you while we investigate.
3. I'll get you a written status update by EOD today (your time), and a root-cause + remediation ETA by tomorrow EOD at the latest — well ahead of your QBR.

If you can share a recent failure timestamp and the workspace_id you're hitting the events endpoint with, that will accelerate triage. Otherwise we'll work from our side.

Thanks for the patience — we'll get you unstuck before Tuesday.

— Robin
TPM, Lumen Analytics

Hi Dani,

Re: audit-log retention (365 vs 90). Before I make the call, I want to make sure I'm not missing context — is there a compliance/contractual driver behind legal's 90-day ask (e.g. data-minimisation under a specific framework), or is it a default conservative posture?

My default lean: go with 90 days for the v1 ship to clear legal's blocker on Monday, and add a configurable retention knob (default 90, max 365) as a fast-follow so we don't lose the enterprise story Morgan is selling. That keeps us shippable and unblocks the spec handoff.

If you're good with that direction I'll update doc.audit_eng_spec and doc.audit_prd today and close out task.AUDIT-6. If you'd rather just pick 90 flat, say the word.

— Robin

Robin — please send me a concise written summary of v2.4 launch
readiness by EOD today: status, risks, what could slip and why,
deploy plan, rollback plan. Three paragraphs is fine.
— Alex

Alex —

Per your ask, here's the Wed EOD readiness snapshot for v2.4 (ship target Fri EOD).

**Status.** On track but with one open P0 risk. RC cut is gated on smoke tests (task.V24-1) and on Maya's migration-under-load validation (task.V24-5). Maya identified a missing workspace_id index on the events table causing ~1-in-5 timeouts during dry-runs; Kai is landing the index fix into RC before cut and Maya is re-running dry-runs against it. Same index gap is the most likely root cause of the BigCorp ETL regression Casey reported on the events endpoint — Kai is investigating and we're tracking customer comms via Jordan/Morgan. Audit-log is parallel track, on schedule for spec review Thu; not gating v2.4.

**Risks / what could slip and why.** (1) Migration validation: if Maya's re-runs against the indexed build still time out, RC slips from Wed to Thu and ship date is at risk — mitigation is the index fix already in flight plus rollback v3 staged. (2) Customer comms (task.V24-4) blocked on sales approval of v24-8; I'll unblock with Morgan tomorrow. (3) Audit-log date-field format (PRD localised vs eng spec UTC) — decision needed Thu with Sam/Priya/Dani; doesn't block v2.4 but blocks AUDIT QA. Retention (90 vs 365) reconcile underway with Legal — tracked on task.AUDIT-6.

**Deploy & rollback.** Friday EOD deploy per runbook v3, post green smoke + clean migration replay in staging. Rollback window is 4h post-deploy (Kai flagged he may want to tighten — I'll confirm with him before Fri); Jordan owns post-deploy customer comms and support rota. I'll send a final go/no-go Fri AM after smoke results.

— Robin

Alex — launch-readiness summary for v2.4 below.

Status: On track for Friday EOD deploy. RC smoke tests in progress (task.V24-1, Kai). Migration validation under load is the critical path: Maya identified a missing workspace_id index on the events table causing ~1-in-5 timeouts in dry-runs; Kai is folding the index fix into the RC and Maya will re-validate (task.V24-5) before the Wed launch-readiness review. Audit-log scaffolding is green but has one open product decision (date-field format on the API — localised vs UTC ISO-8601) that Priya, Sam, Dani and I are resolving this week; it does not block v2.4. Three Morgan-owned deals are gated on audit-log landing in v2.4 scope, which I'm separately confirming with sales (task.OPS-5).

Risks / what could slip and why: (1) Migration index fix — if Maya's re-run is not clean by Wed EOD, we hold the RC cut and slip to Mon at the latest; this is the #1 risk. (2) BigCorp ETL regression on the events endpoint since last Friday's hotfix — acknowledged with Casey, Kai investigating; likely the same workspace_id index gap and should be resolved by the v2.4 fix, but tracked separately. (3) Customer comms (task.V24-4) is blocked on a confirmed deploy window — I'll unblock once smoke + migration are green.

Deploy plan: Cut RC Wed evening after migration re-validation; final smoke Thu AM; deploy Fri during the announced window with Jordan's support coverage rota and runbook v3. Rollback: documented 4-hour window in runbook v3 (task.V24-7, Kai staging), automated revert of the migration plus feature-flag off for audit-log scaffolding. I'll send a written go/no-go after Wed's readiness review.

— Robin

Morgan — on the partner audit-log API contract date:

The customer-facing date-field format (localised vs UTC ISO-8601) is still unresolved between Sam and Priya, and that's a hard blocker for publishing the contract. I've got a 17:00 decision meeting today with Sam, Priya, and Dani as decision-maker to close it.

Assuming the decision lands today, Priya can finalise task.AUDIT-5 (API contract for partners, currently due ~Mon) next week. Realistic date to commit to the partner: **end of next week (one week from Friday)**, contingent on today's call going as planned. I'll confirm a firm date back to you by Wed EOD per your ask.

One related item: you mentioned three closed-won deals gated on audit-log in v2.4 — audit-log is tracking as a *post-v2.4* feature on the board (AUDIT project, separate from V24). I've got task.OPS-5 open to reconcile that with you — can we sync briefly today or tomorrow so I understand what was committed to whom and on what timeline?

— Robin

Morgan — update on the partner audit-log API contract:

Decision is in. At today's 14:00 audit-log spec review (Dani, Priya, Sam, me), we landed:
- API emits ISO-8601 UTC timestamps (Priya owns the eng spec + partner API contract).
- Frontend/UI handles localisation (Sam owns the PRD update).

Both Priya and Sam signed off on the split. Captured in #audit-log and as a comment on doc.audit_prd; PRD + eng spec will be updated this week. Priya can share the partner-facing API contract (task.AUDIT-5) on that basis — I'll nudge her to get you a draft by EOD Fri so you can pass it to the partner.

Net: no change to v2.4 scope, audit-log timeline holds.

Robin

Dani — re: legal review on audit-log retention (eng spec 365d vs legal 90d).

Recommendation: align to 90 days. Rationale:
- Legal has a hard requirement; 365d is an eng-spec default, not a customer commitment.
- Smaller retention shrinks storage/query cost and reduces breach blast-radius.
- None of the three closed-won deals Morgan flagged are gated on >90d retention (will confirm with Morgan, but spec'd at "queryable log of state changes" with no retention SLA in the PRD).
- We can revisit lengthening later if a customer contractually requires it; shortening later is harder.

If you concur, I'll:
1. Update doc.audit_eng_spec to 90 days with a decision note.
2. Add a PRD comment capturing the call.
3. Confirm with Priya so AUDIT-5 (partner API contract) reflects 90d.
4. Reply to legal Monday with the confirmation.

Will proceed unless you push back by EOD Fri. Closing out task.AUDIT-6 once doc is updated.

— Robin

Robin — keep it to one page. Status, biggest risks, next-week
plan. Send by Fri EOD.

Dani — one-pager status for the week. Happy to revise.

## Status
- **v2.4 launch (Fri target):** On track pending two gates — (1) Maya's migration dry-runs under load (events-table workspace_id index gap; Kai aware, fix targeted for RC), and (2) Kai's final smoke pass. Launch readiness review held Wed 14:00; risks logged.
- **Audit-log:** PRD in review with Priya; eng spec contradicts PRD on date-field format. Decision meeting held — landing on ISO-8601 UTC at the API, localisation as a frontend concern. Sam will update PRD; Priya updates eng spec. Retention reconciled (see below).
- **Pipeline refactor RFC:** Decision posted — **defer to Q3** per Kai's recommendation. Q2 capacity stays on v2.4 stabilisation + audit-log.

## Biggest risks
1. **Migration timeouts under load** (events table, ~1/5 in Maya's dry-runs). Mitigation: workspace_id index fix in RC; Maya re-testing pre-Wed. Owner: Kai/Maya.
2. **Audit-log PRD vs eng spec drift** — explicit written decision captured this week to prevent recurrence. Owner: Sam (PRD), Priya (spec).
3. **Customer comms lag** (Q1 retro theme). Jordan's runbook v3 has two opens — post-deploy comms owner + rollback window length. Closing this week.
4. **Retention conflict** — legal wants 90d, eng spec says 365d. Reconciling on 90d to unblock legal handoff Monday; will confirm with Priya/Dani before doc update.

## Next week
- Ship v2.4 Fri; monitor + post-deploy comms (Jordan/Morgan).
- Audit-log: PRD + eng spec updates landed, partner API contract date to Morgan, sales commitment confirmation (OPS-5).

2. **Audit-log scope vs. three gated Q2 deals.** v2.4 ships the audit-log scaffolding only; full feature lands later. Morgan is reconfirming what the deals actually require so we don't over-commit. Will flag immediately if there's a gap.

# Audit-log Engineering Spec

## API
- Endpoint: `GET /v1/audit-log`
- **All timestamps returned in ISO-8601 UTC.** Frontend handles localisation.
- Pagination via cursor.

## Storage
- Append-only table; partitioned weekly.
- Retention: 365 days (under legal review).

## Open question
- Date format must be reconciled with the PRD before integration tests
  can be authored.

# Audit-log PRD

## Goal
Give customer admins a queryable log of state changes affecting their workspace.

## Surface
- Web UI: filterable table.
- **Dates rendered in the user's locale, including in the API response.**
- Export to CSV.

## Retention
- Default 365 days.

## Out of scope
- Per-event diffing (planned for v2.5).

# Audit-log PRD

## Goal
Give customer admins a queryable log of state changes affecting their workspace.

## Surface
- Web UI: filterable table. **Dates rendered in the user's locale in the UI.**
- **API: timestamps returned in ISO-8601 UTC.** Frontend (and partner integrations) are responsible for localising for display.
- Export to CSV (UTC ISO-8601; UI may offer a localised export in a later iteration).

## Retention
- Default 365 days. *Pending legal review — may reduce to 90 days; see task.AUDIT-6.*

## Out of scope
- Per-event diffing (planned for v2.5).

## Decision log
- **t=570 (Mon):** Date format on API = ISO-8601 UTC. Decision made by Dani (VP Eng) in evt.audit_date_decision with Sam (PM), Priya (Eng), Robin (TPM). Rationale: locale-dependent API responses create partner-integration and support burden; UI handles localisation. Supersedes the prior "localised on API" line in this PRD. Sam aligned post-discussion.

- **UI / customer-facing surfaces: localised.** The frontend converts ISO-8601 UTC into the user's locale/timezone for display. Raw UTC must not appear in customer-facing UI.

## First-week priorities

# Data pipeline refactor RFC

## Motivation
Current pipeline is event-batch only; we need streaming for the new
audit-log feature and for the partner integrations Morgan is closing.

## Proposal
Refactor to a Kafka-based ingest with a Postgres sink. Two-quarter
project; Q2 is the earliest possible start.

## Decision needed
- Greenlight Q2 start, or defer to Q3?

## Recommendation
Defer to Q3. Q2 capacity should go to audit-log and v2.4 stabilisation.

# Q1 retro — top three takeaways
1. Migrations are our biggest deploy risk. Always do a load dry-run.
2. Customer comms run late three releases out of four.
3. We over-commit on dates without consulting eng. Stop doing this.

turns.body: Before we dive in — just want to flag that audit-log work is secondary priority right now; v24 ships Friday EOD and that stays the team's main focus. Happy to resolve the date-field format question quickly, but let's timebox this and make sure any decisions don't pull eng bandwidth off v24.

Just to be clear on the business context — I have three deals explicitly gated on the audit-log feature shipping in v2.4, so this isn't a nice-to-have. I'm fully supportive of timeboxing this meeting, but I need confidence that resolving the date-field question today doesn't get deprioritized in a way that risks Friday's scope.

Happy to keep this tight. My position is straightforward: the API contract must emit ISO-8601 UTC — that's non-negotiable for correctness and interoperability. The PRD currently shows a localised format, which belongs in the frontend, not the API layer. If we align on that split today, I can update the eng spec and unblock implementation without touching v24 scope.

Priya, I hear you on ISO-8601 for the API layer — that's actually not in conflict with the PRD if we're precise about it. The PRD says customer-facing surfaces show localized dates; the API can emit ISO-8601 UTC and the frontend converts. What I won't accept is the API becoming the source of truth for display format, because that's how we end up with raw timestamps in the UI. If we document that split explicitly today — API outputs ISO-8601, UI localizes — I can update the PRD to match and we're unblocked.

Before we dive in — Friday EOD is the target we committed to at QBR, so let's be honest about where we actually are. I don't want anyone calling this green until Kai and Jordan have spoken; dates don't get confirmed in this room without the implementing engineers signing off first.

Agreed on waiting for Kai and Jordan before calling it green. On customer comms: I have two enterprise accounts who've already asked about the v2.4 rollout timeline, so if Friday slips or we hit issues post-deploy, I'll need at least a 2-hour heads-up to get ahead of them. v2.4 is green from my side. All critical path items are merged, staging has been clean for 48 hours, and no open P0s. I can walk through the rollback plan when we get to item 3 — it's straightforward, feature-flagged, so we can cut back within minutes if something surfaces post-deploy. Jordan, I'll make sure you get that 2-hour heads-up baked into the runbook.

Sorry to jump in — I don't want to hold things up, but I flagged this to Robin on Monday and I think it needs to be on the table before we call it green. I've been running dry-runs of the v24 prod migration all weekend and it intermittently times out under concurrent write load, roughly 1 in 5 runs. I think the root cause is a missing index — events.workspace_id_idx — during the table-rewrite pass. It's tracked under V24-5. Kai, I really think we need to talk through this before Friday.

Maya, thanks for surfacing V24-5 — I have to be direct: three deals are gated on the audit-log feature in this release, so I can't stay quiet here. A 1-in-5 timeout rate on the prod migration is not a risk I can absorb on the customer side. Kai, can you and Maya confirm today whether that missing index fix is a quick add or a blocker? I need a clear answer before EOD so I know whether to hold my pipeline conversations or start managing expectations now.

Good morning. Top priority this week is v24 — we're targeting Friday EOD, so I want a clear status from each team on blockers before we leave today. Audit log work is secondary; don't let it pull focus from v24 delivery.
v2.4 is on track for Friday EOD. No blockers right now — I'll flag immediately if that changes.

I think the root cause is a missing index on events.workspace_id_idx during the table-rewrite pass, but I need to sync with Kai before we can confirm. I mentioned it to Robin on Monday but wanted to raise it here so it's visible — I don't think we should deploy Friday without resolving it.

Audit log is not pulling any shared resources from v24 this week — we're heads-down on the API spec and won't need infra or DB time until next sprint. Maya, that migration timeout sounds serious; glad you flagged it. Kai, loop me in if you need another set of eyes on the index issue.

ISO-8601 UTC is the right call — locale-dependent API responses are a partner integration nightmare. I'm the named decision-maker: API returns ISO-8601 UTC, UI layer handles localisation. Trade-off is minimal frontend work versus a stable, predictable contract for every consumer. Sam, please update the PRD to match the eng spec and record this decision with my name attached — that's your sign-off. Morgan, tell the partner the contract is ISO-8601 UTC; that should satisfy their Wednesday ask. Let's get this closed today so Priya and QA aren't blocked another day. And just to be clear: this is an audit-log detail — it does not touch v24 scope, so I don't want this meeting bleeding into v24 bandwidth.

Fully aligned with Dani — this matches the eng spec exactly. To be concrete on the trade-off for Sam's PRD note: the only frontend delta is running the UTC timestamp through a locale formatter before display, which is a one-liner in any modern i18n library. That's the documented cost. Sam, if it helps, I can drop the exact wording into doc.audit_prd as a comment so you just need to approve it rather than draft from scratch.

I want to be on record: the PRD reflects my position that the API should return localised dates because ISO-8601 UTC is jargon to end customers reading audit logs directly. That said, Dani is the named decision-maker and the trade-off is documented — partner contract stability outweighs the customer-facing concern here, and Priya's one-liner localisation cost is real. I'll accept the flip on one condition: doc.audit_prd must explicitly note that the UI *must* localise before display, no exceptions, so we don't silently regress on the customer experience. Sam, if Priya drafts the comment, I'd like a quick review pass before you approve it to make sure the localisation requirement is unambiguous.
